findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed sanitizer at the bar’s triple sink to not be reaching the sanitizing concentration benchmark set by the manufacturer’s label (200-400 ppm of quaternary ammonia). CORRECTED- PIC made bleach water sanitizer at a concentration of 200 ppm. Inspector will return on 10/30/25 to check one of two solutions:
1) The facility has adjusted the water heater to reach 75F to allow quaternary ammonia sanitizer tablets to dissolve.
2) Facility has obtained unscented bleach (with an EPA registration number and label indicating use for food contact surfaces) to use as sanitizer. Facility has test strips for both sanitizers, so either are acceptable means of sanitation for food contact surfaces.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions. [P]

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Inspector observed two temperature control for food safety (TCS) food items (orange juice and heavy whipping cream) to be without date marking in the facility. CORRECTED- the heavy whipping cream was voluntarily discarded by the person in charge (PIC), and the orange juice was labeled with a date. Ensure all TCS food and drinks are marked with a date once opened; the day the item is opened counts as “day one”. Use or discard within seven days.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A). [P]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Inspector observed container holding multiple food contact utensils at the bar to be soiled with debris. CORRECTED- PIC cleaned and sanitized cup holding utensils. Ensure all nonfood contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of debris, which may transfer to food contact surfaces.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: SECOND REPEAT: Fan covers in the walk in cooler were observed to be soiled with dust and ice. Nonfood contact surfaces should be cleaned at a frequency to prevent the buildup of debris. Clean fans during defrost. Inspector will check the cleaning of the fans during a spot check on 10/30/25.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. [C]

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
Signed reporting agreements are not on file. Inspector provided a blank reporting agreement. Make copies so that staff can review and sign. Keep signed reporting agreements on file for review during health inspections. Inspector will follow up to see signed reporting agreements.
2-103.11: (O) FOOD EMPLOYEES are informed in verifiable manner of their responsibility to report accordance with LAW, to PIC, information about their health related to disease transmissible through FOOD.  [Pf]

findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
findings.comment:
Facility does not have a clean up policy in place for vomit/diarrhea. CORRECTED- Inspector printed a vomit/diarrhea clean up policy. Post or keep policy on file for review in case its needed.
2-501.11: A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. Reference 2-501.11.  [Pf]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
Bartender observed to turn the faucet off without using a barrier. Use a paper towel or other barrier to turn the faucet off after washing hands to prevent recontamination of clean hands.
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED. [P]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
Paper towel dispenser in the mens restroom was not working. Paper towels are in the machine, but they are not being dispensed. CORRECTED- PIC placed a roll of paper towels in the restroom. Ensure paper towels are always available at all handwashing sinks.
6-301.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. [Pf]

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
Quat test strips appear to be damaged and are not registering sanitizer concentration. Purchase new test strips. Keep them in a dry location.
4-302.14: A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided. [Pf]

findings.title: Toilet facilities: properly constructed, supplied, & cleaned
findings.comment:
Neither of the restroom doors are self-closing. Add self closers to the restroom doors.
6-202.14: Toilet rooms located on PREMISES shall be completely enclosed and provided with tightfitting and self-closing door. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
WALK-IN COOLER: 1. Door trim in the walk-in cooler was soiled with mold. Clean inside the walk-in cooler.
2. Ceiling and fan covers were soiled with what appeared to be general buildup of dust. Clean the ceiling and fan covers in the walk-in cooler.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 & 6-501.12 Physical facilities shall be maintained in good repair, and cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. [C]

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
Bartender working at time of inspection had a food handler certificate that expired earlier this year. She is enrolled to renew the certificate. Employees need to complete an online food handler certification course that is ANSI and IL approved. Copies of certifications need to be maintained on-site.
410 ILCS 625  Sec. 3.06  All food handlers, other than someone who has a food manager certification, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.11 & 6-501.12 WALK-IN COOLER: 1. Door trim in the walk-in cooler was soiled with mold. Inner door trim was also unsealed and had exposed insulation. Clean inside the walk-in cooler and provide a proper seal for the inner door frame of the walk-in cooler.
2. Ceiling and fan covers were soiled with what appeared to be general buildup of dust. Clean the ceiling and fan covers in the walk-in cooler.
ICE MACHINE ROOM: 1. Baseboard was loose at the floor to wall juncture by the ice machine. Repair or replace the loose coving.
2. Wall had a hole in it next to the ice machine in the same area where baseboard was loose. Repair the wall.
Physical facilities shall be maintained in good repair, and cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text:
3-304.11 Mold accumulation was observed in the ice machine. Buildup was present along the top of the baffle behind the lid. A significant amount was observed on the ceiling behind the baffle. 
-Ice scoop was stored in a covered, plastic container that was soiled with grimy buildup. 
Follow-up inspection will be conducted on 12/6/21 to verify the ice machine and ice scoop storage container have been properly cleaned and sanitized.
Food shall only contact surfaces of equipment and utensils that are cleaned and sanitized as specified under Parts 4-6 and 4-7 of the 2017 FDA Food Code.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.citation_text:
4-302.14 Quat test kit was observed sealed in foil packaging and had an expiration date of 2018. Obtain a new test kit and ensure it is being used to verify concentration of sanitizer solutions. 
A test kit that accurately measures the concentration of sanitizing solutions in mg/L shall be provided.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.citation_text:
4-303.11 Sanitizer solution was not available for use at the time of inspection. Sanitizer preparation and availability during hours of operation were discussed.
Sanitizer shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.11 & 6-501.12 WALK-IN COOLER: 1. Step inside the walk-in cooler was damaged. Trim was documented to be damaged at the 2018 routine inspection. Provide proper repairs to the step inside the cooler.
2. Door trim in the walk-in cooler was soiled with mold. Inner door trim was also unsealed and had exposed insulation. Clean inside the walk-in cooler and provide a proper seal for the inner door frame of the walk-in cooler.
3. Ceiling and fan covers were soiled with what appeared to be general buildup of dust. Clean the ceiling and fan covers in the walk-in cooler.
ICE MACHINE ROOM: 1. Baseboard was loose at the floor to wall juncture by the ice machine. Repair or replace the loose coving.
2. Wall had a hole in it next to the ice machine in the same area where baseboard was loose. Repair the wall.
Physical facilities shall be maintained in good repair, and cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625  Sec. 3.06 Bartender working at time of inspection did not have a food handler certification. Foodhandler FAQ and options for course information were provided. Employees need to complete an online food handler certification course that is ANSI and IL approved. Copies of certifications need to be maintained on-site.
All food handlers, other than someone who has a food manager certification, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code.
